obligation.what: At a choice ORDINAL comparison (`<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` whose operands are `choice` values), every operand's declared choice type must carry the `ordered` modifier. Ordinal comparison of an unordered choice set has no defined order, so the operation is unsafe unless every operand is declared ordered.
obligation.duType: ModifierRequirement(Subject: ParamSubject(PChoice), Required: ModifierKind.Ordered, Description: "Both choice operands must be declared ordered")

mintSites.howMinted: Catalog-declared on BinaryOperationMeta.ProofRequirements for the four choice ordinal operators: ChoiceLessThanChoice (:871), ChoiceGreaterThanChoice (:879), ChoiceLessThanOrEqualChoice (:887), ChoiceGreaterThanOrEqualChoice (:895). Each declares one ModifierRequirement(ParamSubject(PChoice), ModifierKind.Ordered). The equality operators ChoiceEqualsChoice/ChoiceNotEqualsChoice (:860,:863) declare NO ProofRequirements — equality needs no order, so `==`/`!=` on choice never mints a Modifier obligation.
mintSites.instantiatedAt: src/Precept/Pipeline/ProofEngine.cs:305-310 (TypedBinaryOp arm: `foreach (var req in bin.ProofRequirements) obligations.Add(new ProofObligation(req, bin, ctx, ProofDisposition.Unresolved, null, null))`). This is the ONLY mint path for Modifier — the kind is catalog-declared on binary operators only and is never synthesized elsewhere in ProofEngine.cs / ProofEngine.Analysis.cs. A grep for `new ModifierRequirement` across src/Precept confirms the four Operations.cs sites are the complete set.

mintCompleteness: For ProofRequirementKind.Modifier the catalog IS the complete mint surface: the only obligation carrier is BinaryOperationMeta.ProofRequirements at the four ordinal-operator sites, and the only ModifierKind ever required is Ordered. Unlike Numeric/Presence/Count/Length/Index kinds (which are synthesized by the engine with no catalog site), Modifier has no synthesized mint path. This was confirmed against source, not assumed from the catalog.

premiseClasses: (a) field modifiers — the ONLY applicable class
dischargeShape.whyOnlyClassA: The `ordered` modifier is a declaration-time STRUCTURAL property of the operand's choice TYPE, not a fact about its runtime VALUE. Premise classes (b) arg constraints, (c) handler guard, and (d) pre-state constraint/inductive hypothesis all supply VALUE facts (`x != 0`, `x >= 0`, `Total_pre <= 1000`). None can make a field's declared type ordered — orderedness is fixed by the `ordered` keyword in the type declaration and no guard, argument value, or pre-state value can supply it. So classes (b)/(c)/(d) are structurally inapplicable to this obligation, and the applicable-class set is the singleton {(a)}. (Note: when an operand is an event arg of an ordered choice type, the modifier still rides on the arg's DECLARED type — structurally class-(a)-shaped even though the operand is an argument; the discharge reads the declaration, not an ingress value fact.)
dischargeShape.iff: The obligation discharges IFF every operand of the ordinal comparison resolves to a declared `choice` type that carries the `ordered` modifier (equivalently: the operand's TypedChoiceElement.Ordered == true, or the operand field's Modifiers contains ModifierKind.Ordered). Not RHS-only — the definition is BOTH operands. (The shipped compiler under-checks this; see knownCompilerHoles.)
dischargeShape.decisionProcedure: Bounded structural membership check over the (at most two) operand positions of the comparison. For each operand: resolve it to its declared choice type and test `ModifierKind.Ordered ∈ declaredModifiers` or `TypedChoiceElement.Ordered == true`. No search, no fixpoint, no interval arithmetic, no guard normal-form matching. The bound is the operand arity (2). This satisfies the ratification gate's 'name the decision procedure / search bound' requirement: the reject side is decided by a finite two-operand membership test.
dischargeShape.notArgumentLess: The derivation cites the generative rule 'a declared field/type modifier is a licensed class-(a) premise' plus the structural-fact validity argument below; both carry subjects (the operand field, the `ordered` declaration). No cell here rests on an argument-less rule.

transport.fact: phi = 'operand O's declared choice type carries `ordered`'
transport.readClosure: deps(phi) = empty. The fact reads NO field value — it is a property of the declaration, not of any configuration's field contents.
transport.killable: never. Under the transport rule (transport-rule-restatement-2026-07-21.md § 5 provenance table), a fact whose read-closure is empty is never killed: `mayWrite(r, p, q) ∩ deps(phi) = mayWrite(r,p,q) ∩ empty = empty` on every route r and every position pair, so the frame condition is trivially satisfied. This is the same row as 'Literal denotation … killable: never; read-closure empty' and 'Catalog-declared callee attribute … the attribute is not [killable]' in that table.
transport.availableOnEveryRoute: Because it is earned at declaration time and never killed, the fact is available at position zero of every route and at every evaluation occasion. Transport is therefore INERT for this kind: the route/occasion axis does not change the discharge. All five occasions below discharge identically from the same structural fact; the near-miss fails all five occasions identically. The site-identity ruling (one expression reached by N routes mints N obligations) still applies to COUNTING obligations, but every one of those N obligations discharges from the same route-invariant `ordered` declaration.
transport.citation: transport-rule-restatement-2026-07-21.md § 5, 'Literal denotation … never; read-closure empty' and the catalog-attribute row; matrix § Vocabulary, 'Discharge mechanisms'.

citationDuty.ruling: matrix § The cell, owner ruling 2026-07-21: 'A declared constraint or field modifier is available as a premise for a fault obligation, and a proof may not consume such a fact unless it names the obligation that established the fact and every obligation that preserves it, each itself discharged … class (a) is not exempt from it.'
citationDuty.derivedApplication: For a VALUE modifier (`positive`, `nonzero`) the establishing obligation is establishment-at-construction and the preserving obligations are preservation-at-every-write-site of every mentioning field. For the `ordered` STRUCTURAL modifier those obligations are vacuous: (establishing) the `ordered` keyword on the choice type is checked once at parse/type-check and is the establishment; (preserving) the preserving-obligation set is EMPTY because no write can change a field's declared type — the fact has empty read-closure (see transport) so nothing preserves-or-breaks it. Under this reading the citation duty is discharged by naming 'declaration of `ordered` on the operand's choice type; preserving set = empty (type-structural, immutable across all writes)'.
citationDuty.flagged: Whether the citation duty is SATISFIED by an empty preserving set (as derived above) or whether a structural/type modifier is simply OUTSIDE the citation duty is NOT explicitly ruled. The ruling's own language ('a field modifier is a constraint on one field, and its truth at an evaluation site is earned the same way') presumes a VALUE constraint earned by establishment+preservation; `ordered` constrains type structure, not value, and is not earned that way. See openFlags.

respellability.band: The sound-but-unprovable band is EMPTY for this kind. A choice ordinal comparison whose operand is not declared `ordered` is not merely unprovable — it is genuinely unsafe by definition (an unordered choice set has no defined ordinal order), so rejecting it is correct, not conservative. There is no sound program the rules cannot prove.
respellability.respelling: The suggestion schema is 'add `ordered` to the declaration of ⟨deficient operand's choice type⟩' — naming every operand that lacks it. This is a declaration edit, not a proof-power widening, and the want doc's 'forces authors to be more explicit' friction applies in its lightest form (a one-keyword edit).
respellability.familyInheritance: This is a per-cell verdict identical across all five occasions, inherited from the single-premise-class structural shape; no cell overrides it.

knownCompilerHoles.severity: soundness hole (shipped compiler accepts a program the definition rejects)
knownCompilerHoles.description: The shipped discharge verifies ONLY the right-hand operand's `ordered` bit. ResolveParamInBinaryOp (src/Precept/Pipeline/ProofEngine.cs:878-889) checks the Rhs parameter first and returns bin.Right; TryDeclarationAttributeProof then discharges on that single resolved operand. When the LEFT operand is unordered and the RIGHT is ordered, the obligation is wrongly reported Proved/DeclarationAttribute even though the definition requires BOTH ordered.
knownCompilerHoles.witnessToHole: precept `ModLeftDeficient` (verified 2026-07-21): `rule Urgency >= Severity` with Urgency (LEFT) NOT ordered and Severity (RIGHT) ordered compiles clean, 0 diagnostics, obligation disposition Proved, strategy DeclarationAttribute. Contrast `ModBothDeficient` (both unordered) and every RHS-deficient near-miss below, which correctly reject PRE0112.
knownCompilerHoles.consequenceForCells: The near-miss rows in the four scalar cells are VERIFIED-REJECTING only because they place the deficient operand on the RHS. A left-deficient variant of each would wrongly compile. The cells record the definition's contract (BOTH operands, iff) and flag that shipped enforcement is RHS-only.

knownCompilerHoles.severity: soundness hole + false-reject hole (both polarities broken for a quantifier-binding operand)
knownCompilerHoles.description: When an operand is a quantifier binding `x` (from `each x in C (...)`), the `ordered` bit of C's inner choice type is not correctly consulted through the modifier discharge. Two broken directions were observed: (1) with the binding on the LEFT (`x >= Severity`), the RHS-only hole above means only Severity is checked, so the ObservedLevels-not-ordered near-miss wrongly proves; (2) with the binding on the RIGHT (`Severity <= x`), the engine resolves the subject to `x`, cannot confirm x's ordered bit even when C IS declared ordered, and FALSE-REJECTS with PRE0112 'Cannot prove that x satisfies … Ordered'.
knownCompilerHoles.witnessToHole: verified 2026-07-21: `ModQuantifierNearMiss` (binding LEFT, C unordered) -> wrongly Proved; `ModQuantRhsWitness` (binding RIGHT, C ORDERED) -> wrongly rejected PRE0112 on x.
knownCompilerHoles.compoundedBy: collection-types.md § Implementation state: quantifier predicates (each/any/no) are 'Not yet built' as runtime governance rules. So the quantifier occasion rests on an unbuilt feature at runtime AND on two live compile-time holes.

keyFindings: Modifier is the one fault kind whose ONLY premise class is (a) field modifiers and whose discharge is non-transportable/non-killable (structural, not a value fact).

openFlags: CITATION-DUTY-SCOPE: The matrix § The cell (2026-07-21) citation duty presumes a VALUE constraint earned by establishment-at-construction + preservation-at-every-write. The `ordered` modifier is a type-STRUCTURAL property with empty read-closure — it has no value to establish or preserve. Whether the duty is discharged by an empty preserving set (declaration = establishment, nothing preserves) or whether structural modifiers are OUTSIDE the duty entirely is not ruled. Needs an owner ruling; the cells give the derivable empty-preserving-set reading but do not treat it as settled.

COMPILER-HOLE (route to bugs.md / build): the Modifier discharge verifies only the RHS operand's `ordered` bit (ResolveParamInBinaryOp checks Rhs first and returns; TryDeclarationAttributeProof discharges on the single resolved operand). Definition requires BOTH operands. Witness of unsoundness: ModLeftDeficient (`rule Urgency >= Severity`, Urgency unordered on LEFT) compiles clean, Proved. This is a P11/prevention breach for the Modifier kind and blocks ratification of every Modifier near-miss as a complete both-operands check.
